title: EU public confidence combines institutional support and security alignment with persistent cost-of-living pressure and uneven democratic satisfaction
source_unit: European Commission, Standard Eurobarometer 105: Spring 2026, fieldwork March-April 2026 and publication May 2026
geography: European Union citizens across the 27 Member States, with country factsheets and wider coverage in the Eurobarometer dataset

observations.period: Spring 2026; EU trust, democracy, and membership

denominator.unit: Standard Eurobarometer 105 EU27 public-opinion survey frame

democracy_satisfaction.unit: percent of EU citizens satisfied with the way democracy works in the EU

membership_benefit.unit: percent believing their country has benefited overall from EU membership

eu_stability.unit: percent agreeing the EU is a place of stability in a troubled world

eu_trust.unit: percent trusting the EU, up 3 percentage points from autumn 2025

legitimacy_route.value: support for EU membership and stability coexists with a more moderate level of satisfaction with how EU democracy works

observations.method: European Commission Standard Eurobarometer 105 public-opinion survey conducted across the EU27, with national factsheets and trend comparisons.
observations.uncertainty: Aggregate EU averages conceal substantial country and subgroup variation; trust and satisfaction are attitudes, not direct measures of institutional performance or democratic quality.
observations.subgroup: EU citizens, national publics, EU institutions, member-state governments, voters, and people evaluating membership and democratic responsiveness.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stability and membership support may be driven by external insecurity or practical benefits without implying durable trust in all EU institutions or policies.

observations.period: Spring 2026; security, Ukraine, and common defense

denominator.unit: Standard Eurobarometer 105 EU27 public-opinion survey frame

common_defense.unit: percent backing a common defense and security policy among Member States

russia_threat.unit: percent agreeing Russia's invasion of Ukraine is a threat to EU security

eu_response_satisfaction.unit: percent satisfied with the EU's response to Russia's invasion of Ukraine

ukraine_support.unit: percent agreeing the EU should continue supporting Ukraine until a just and lasting peace

security_route.value: external geopolitical threat is associated with unusually high support for shared defense and continued Ukraine support

observations.method: EU27 Standard Eurobarometer public-opinion survey with security and external-relations questions.
observations.uncertainty: The measures record public attitudes at one fieldwork point and do not identify whether support reflects threat perception, solidarity, strategic preference, or partisan and national differences.
observations.subgroup: EU citizens, national governments, EU institutions, defense publics, Ukraine-support constituencies, and populations exposed to war-related information.
observations.counterinterpretation: High support for common defense or Ukraine assistance may weaken if costs, escalation concerns, or national political conditions change; opinion does not establish policy capacity.

observations.period: Spring 2026; cost of living and economic expectations

denominator.unit: Standard Eurobarometer 105 EU27 public-opinion survey frame

national_cost_concern.unit: percent identifying cost of living among the main issues facing their country

personal_cost_concern.unit: percent identifying cost of living among the main issues facing them personally

eu_economy_good.unit: percent considering the EU economic situation good

economic_stability_expectation.value: 42 percent think the European economic situation will remain the same over the next 12 months, 36 percent think it will worsen, and 15 percent think it will improve

material_legitimacy_route.value: institutional support and geopolitical alignment are being evaluated alongside direct household cost pressure and weak economic optimism

observations.method: EU27 Standard Eurobarometer survey questions on personal, national, and EU-level concerns and economic expectations.
observations.uncertainty: Concern rankings are not household expenditure measures or causal drivers of trust; EU-level averages obscure income, country, housing, and energy-exposure differences.
observations.subgroup: Households, lower-income residents, consumers, workers, national publics, EU economic policymakers, and groups exposed to price and energy volatility.
observations.counterinterpretation: High concern can coexist with adaptive behavior, improving real incomes, or strong institutional support; negative expectations do not necessarily translate into political change.

observations.period: Spring 2026; currency and EU future orientation

denominator.unit: Standard Eurobarometer 105 EU27 public-opinion survey frame

euro_support.unit: percent supporting the euro across the EU, the highest level since its introduction

euro_area_support.unit: percent in the euro area supporting the common currency

future_optimism.unit: approximate share of Europeans saying they are optimistic about the future of the EU

international_concern.value: the Middle East conflict, broader international situation, and Russia's war against Ukraine were the top EU-level concerns

cohesion_route.value: shared currency and future orientation remain relatively strong anchors even as security and cost pressures shape public judgment

observations.method: EU27 Standard Eurobarometer survey with trend measures for euro support, optimism, and EU-level issues.
observations.uncertainty: Support and optimism are aggregate attitudes, not forecasts of economic integration or policy consensus; the report does not explain which groups or experiences account for the changes.
observations.subgroup: Euro-area and non-euro EU citizens, households, workers, businesses, EU institutions, and publics evaluating international risk.
observations.counterinterpretation: Symbolic support for the euro or EU future can coexist with dissatisfaction over policy delivery, redistribution, or national economic conditions.

related_sources.claim: The European Data Portal provides the Standard Eurobarometer STD105 dataset and downloadable data resources.
The Eurobarometer survey detail page provides first results, data annexes, country factsheets, and report documents.

boundary: This record adds current EU public-opinion evidence on democratic satisfaction, trust, EU membership, security, Ukraine, cost of living, economic expectations, euro support, and future optimism. It is aggregate cross-national survey evidence, not respondent-level ingestion, a causal trust model, a security forecast, or proof that EU support is evenly distributed across countries and social groups.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official European Commission Eurobarometer page and data-portal summary reviewed for fieldwork timing, EU trust and democracy, membership benefit, stability, Ukraine and defense, cost-of-living, economic expectations, euro support, and optimism measures.
